guide_companion_description: Bitfocus Companion controls Autona through the External Control API over HTTP. Map physical buttons to the operations below.
guide_companion_step_1: Launch Companion and open its web admin page (default http://127.0.0.1:8000).
guide_companion_step_3: Select a button, then "Add action" and choose the Generic HTTP "POST" (or "GET") action.
guide_companion_step_4: Paste the request URL from the table below. For POST, set the body to the JSON shown and add the header Content-Type: application/json.
guide_companion_step_5: If Companion runs on another PC (LAN access), also add the header X-Autona-Token with the access token as its value. Copy the token from Help & Settings → API Settings → Open reference & tester.
guide_companion_step_6: Optionally set the button text, then press the key to test.
guide_companion_lan_lan: This device must be on the same LAN as this PC.
guide_companion_lan_lanAtRestart: LAN access: saved as on, takes effect when Autona is restarted — until then other devices cannot connect.
guide_companion_lan_off: LAN access: disabled — other devices cannot connect. Enable it under Settings → Network (restart required).
guide_companion_icons_hint: Click an icon to copy it to the clipboard, then paste it onto a Companion button.
guide_companion_icons_no_copy: This page cannot put images on the clipboard (a page from another computer over http). Right-click an icon to save it, then set it on a Companion button.
guide_obs_description: Set up integration between OBS Studio's Advanced Scene Switcher plugin and Autona.
guide_obs_lan_lan: OBS must run on this PC. For OBS on another PC on the same LAN, replace 127.0.0.1 with this PC's IP address and add ?token=<access token> to the end of the URL (&token=<access token> if the URL already has a ?; copy the token from API Settings → Open reference & tester).
guide_obs_lan_lanAtRestart: LAN access: saved as on, takes effect when Autona is restarted — until then OBS must run on this PC.
guide_obs_lan_off: LAN access: disabled — OBS must run on this PC. To use OBS on another PC, enable it under Settings → Network (restart required).
guide_obs_http_title: Control Autona from Advanced Scene Switcher
guide_obs_http_step_1: In OBS, open Tools -> Advanced Scene Switcher -> Macros and add a macro.
guide_obs_http_step_2: Add a trigger (e.g. Hotkey, Scene, or WebSocket message).
guide_obs_http_step_3: Add an action -> HTTP, paste the URL from the table below, and set the method to POST.
guide_obs_http_step_4: If the table lists a body, paste it into the body field. Leave Content-Type at its default (application/json).
guide_obs_http_step_5: Save and trigger the condition to test.
guide_obs_http_version_note: Requires Advanced Scene Switcher 1.30 or newer (HTTP action with a Content-Type field). The action also stores the response status and body in temporary variables, usable in follow-up conditions.
guide_obs_destructive_note: Destructive operations (clear / reset) require "confirm": true in the JSON body. See the API reference page for the full catalogue.
guide_obs_watch_step_1: In OBS, open Tools -> Advanced Scene Switcher -> Macros and add a macro.
guide_obs_watch_step_2: Add a condition -> File, then browse to one of the files below (use Copy file path to get the absolute path).
guide_obs_watch_step_3: Choose the match mode: exact content / regex for a *.txt value, or "File was modified" on program_state.json to react to any change.
guide_obs_watch_step_4: Add an action -> Switch scene and pick the target scene.
guide_obs_export_note: Keep text export enabled (Settings: general.disable_export must be off).
guide_obs_paths_this_pc_only: Absolute paths are shown on this PC only; below are the paths inside Autona's folder.
guide_obs_watch_note: *.txt files hold the raw value (easy to match). program_state.json carries revision/timestamp, so watch it for "file modified" to react to any state change.
